t: A Malay Muslim sultanate on the northwest coast of Borneo whose rulers trace a line back to the fourteenth century.
Around 1500 its fleets and allies made it the leading power of Borneo's coasts and the southern Philippines.
It lost most of its lands to Sarawak and Britain but survived as a protectorate and, from 1984, an independent state.
dyk: A king of Po-ni, early Brunei, died during a visit to the Ming court in 1408, and his tomb can still be visited in Nanjing.
ev: A king of Po-ni visits the Ming court at Nanjing and dies there
Antonio Pigafetta describes the water city of Brunei
Spain captures the capital in the Castilian War but soon withdraws
Sarawak is granted to James Brooke
Brunei becomes fully independent under Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah

f.capital: Kota Batu; later Brunei Town (Bandar Seri Begawan since 1970)
f.founder: Muhammad Shah (Awang Alak Betatar), according to tradition
